title: Can Dogs Eat Chocolate: Mild Signs Can Start at 9 mg Per Pound 🍫 (Things Living In Your House)
description:
Can dogs eat chocolate? The FDA says chocolate is toxic to dogs, and that theobromine is the main culprit. Theobromine can cause mild signs in dogs with doses as low as 9 mg per pound of body weight, and severe signs starting around 18 mg per pound. That dose is per pound of the dog's body weight, so the same amount can be milder for a large dog and severe for a small one. The same FDA table lists about 57 mg of theobromine in an ounce of milk chocolate, and about 227 mg in dark chocolate with 70-85% cacao. Do not say any amount is safe, and do not say a bite always kills. The ASPCA says cats are also sensitive to theobromine, though they tend not to eat as much chocolate. If your pet is sick or has a veterinary emergency, call your veterinarian. If your veterinarian is unavailable, call your local emergency animal hospital or an animal poison control center.
